text: We tested a weak-to-strong generalization method that selects training examples by agreement between weak labels and the strong model's embedding geometry, retaining a select_fraction of 0.6, with pythia-410m as the weak supervisor and qwen2.5-3b as the strong student. Across 6 seeds, the method reached a performance gap recovered (PGR) of 0.38 with a standard error of 0.04, against a baseline PGR of 0.21; the margin over the baseline exceeds two standard errors of the measured PGR. Transfer accuracy was 0.72 with a standard error of 0.01, sitting between the weak supervisor's accuracy of 0.63 and the strong model's ceiling of 0.88, so the student surpasses its teacher but remains well short of fully supervised strong performance. Two caveats temper the reading: no standard error is reported for the baseline PGR, so the comparison rests on the method's variance alone, and the evidence comes from a single weak-strong model pair at one selection fraction.
